plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the clock mechanism ensures the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point (bid) determines when I drop out. Since payment depends only on others' bids, not my own, bidding truthfully (my actual value) is a dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $22.

This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by exit points on the clock. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy - it ensures you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses). With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $15.

Since the payment rule mirrors a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), bidding my true value is weakly optimal—it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing value unnecessarily. With a value of $10, bidding exactly $10 ensures I win only when profitable (when others' bids are below $10) and lose otherwise, paying the second-highest bid which will always be less than my value if I win.
